newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Egypt's Mubarak says European task force much debated.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's Mubarak says European task force much debated.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on Tuesday said after visits to Tunisia and Libya that an intervention force known as Eurofor announced by four European countries worried south Mediterranean states.

"I fear that it (the Eurofor plan) opens the way to interference in (other states) internal affairs," Mubarak told a news conference in Tunis after talks with Tunisian President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali.
"The issue needs explanations," he added in the first Egyptian official stand on Eurofor plan.
The European countries had said that the force was designed to be used for peacekeeping and humanitarian missions in conflicts like the one currently devastating eastern Zaire.

The force will be able to call on up to 10,000 troops for use and has its command headquarters in Florence, Italy. It will be made available to the 10-nation Western European Union and can also be put at the disposal of NATO and the United Nations, the countries involved have said.

During Mubarak's visit to Tripoli the force -- constituted last month by Italy, Spain, France and Portugal -- dominated talks with Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi, the official Libyan news agency JANA reported.

"The announcement on the setting up by Italy, France, Spain and Portugal of an European land and navy force was one of the most important issues discussed...," Libyan Pan-Arab Unity Affairs Minister Jomaa al-Fezzani said.

Tunisia deplored that the Eurofor was set up without prior consultations with southern Mediterranean countries, but did not mention the issue namely among "the regional and international issues" discussed by Ben Ali and Mubarak.
Mubarak travelled by land from Libya to Tunisia on Tuesday.

A U.N. embargo bans air travel to and from Libya. The travel restrictions are aimed at forcing Libya to hand over two of its citizens wanted for the bombing of a Pan Am airliner over Lockerbie, Scotland in 1988.
